title: Reduce metrics cardinality for route experiment dimensions (limited tags + sampled expansions)
author: Logan Wright
release_notes:
- Reduced default tag cardinality for experiment-attributed metrics to prevent metrics cost spikes in high-route-count accounts.
- Added sampled “expanded” metrics with model_id/region for debugging without blowing up series count.
- Added drop counters and dashboards can use new tag keys (route_norm_id).
description:
Context: As we ramp Route-level Experiments beta traffic, we’ve seen two recurring issues: (1) high time-series explosion when tagging high-volume metrics with {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region}, and (2) query cost spikes in Console results views that join on raw route identifiers. This PR adjusts the default metrics tagging strategy to keep the canonical attribution (experiment_id + variant_id) while constraining high-cardinality dimensions and providing a sampled path for deeper drilldowns.

What changed (high level): We now treat experiment attribution as two tiers: Tier A (always-on) and Tier B (sampled expansion). Tier A is used for all request + token hot-path counters/histograms and includes: experiment_id, variant_id, route_norm_id (normalized/template route identifier, not raw path), and deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private). Tier B is emitted at a configurable sampling rate (default 1%) and includes the additional high-cardinality dimensions: model_id and region. The sampling is deterministic per request using the same request_id hash, so charts remain stable over time.

Motivation / prior incidents: In staging we hit a metrics pipeline outage after expanding tags (see incident thread 1738710922 and the Gmail thread on cardinality risk review). We also saw Console results query cost spikes tied to per-route dimensionality (thread 1738798031). This PR is the follow-up to keep our beta/GA posture safe by default.

Implementation details: 1) Introduced route_norm_id: router now emits route_norm_id derived from the route template key already used for policy evaluation (e.g., "/v1/chat/completions" + route UUID), and explicitly does NOT emit raw paths as a metrics label. 2) Added an allowlisted experiment tag set for hot metrics: the metrics registry now enforces a fixed label set for experiment-attributed series and will drop/strip disallowed labels rather than emitting them. 3) Added sampled expanded metrics: for a small, deterministic sample we emit separate metric names suffixed with ".expanded" that include model_id + region. 4) Added visibility: new counters track how often labels were stripped (experiment_label_stripped_total) and how often expanded metrics were emitted (experiment_metrics_expanded_emitted_total) so we can validate sampling and detect accidental regressions.

Operational impact: This reduces series count substantially in accounts with many routes and/or multi-region usage. Console results will continue to use rollups keyed by {route_norm_id, experiment_id, variant_id}. Model/region drilldowns are still possible but are intended for debugging and sampled validation, not as the default UI slice for GA (see design notes in the cardinality thread).

Testing: Added unit tests for tag allowlisting and deterministic sampling; validated locally with otel-collector + prometheus and verified that label stripping increments when model_id is attempted on Tier A metrics. Ran a synthetic load test (internal tool) against staging and confirmed series count stays flat as routes scale up. CI includes an existing flaky OTel exporter test; reran once.

Rollout plan: Safe to ship behind our existing route experiments feature flag; this change only affects label sets / metric names. SRE will monitor (a) experiment_label_stripped_total (should be near 0 outside of accidental tagging) and (b) overall active series for experiment.* metrics. If needed, sampling rate is a dynamic config (no restart) with default 1%.

Notes: This PR intentionally does not change the analytics rollup schema; that migration is tracked separately. Also, this does not introduce any stat-sig analysis (explicit GA non-goal).
commits: telemetry: add allowlisted experiment label set for hot-path metrics
router: emit route_norm_id for experiment attribution (avoid raw path labels)
telemetry: deterministic sampling for expanded experiment metrics
metrics: add stripped-label and expanded-emission counters
tests: cover allowlisting and sampling determinism
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm Console doesn’t rely on model_id/region tags for the default results page? Losing those dimensions on primary metrics is fine, but we should keep a path for debugging and avoid changing label keys without a breadcrumb.

Logan Wright (author): Confirmed with Felix/Jada: default results are keyed by {route, experiment_id, variant_id}. Added explicit ".expanded" metrics with deterministic 1% sampling for model_id/region and added strip counters so we can detect accidental tag attempts. Also added route_norm_id naming to avoid raw path labels.

Sean Gallagher (review): +1 on allowlist. Please include a concrete estimate of series reduction and make sure there’s a kill-switch if expanded metrics still cause issues. Also make sure this won’t break existing alerts/dashboards.

Logan Wright (author): Added dynamic config for expanded sampling rate (0 disables). Series reduction in staging synthetic test: ~28x fewer active series for experiment-attributed token metrics when varying routes/models/regions. Dashboard updates are in a separate observability-pack PR; for this PR we’re only changing redwood emission.
Nadia Rahman (review): For cost/token, are we still emitting the same counters needed by the cost attribution pipeline? I’m worried about dropping model_id on Tier A if the cost pipeline expects it.

Logan Wright (author): Cost pipeline uses request context fields and rollups, not raw metric tags. Tier A keeps experiment_id/variant_id + route_norm_id; model_id remains present in traces and in sampled expanded metrics for sanity checks. Caleb and I verified the rollup job inputs are unaffected.

Caleb Johnson (review): Please ensure the label stripping happens before export to avoid cardinality blowups at the collector. Also, can we log once per minute when stripping occurs so oncall can find it quickly?

Logan Wright (author): Stripping is in-process in the metrics wrapper (pre-OTel export). Added counters; avoided logs by default to prevent log spam, but we can add a rate-limited warn in a follow-up if SRE wants it.
Allison Grant (approval): Looks good with the sampled expansion + route_norm_id. Please add a short note to the internal runbook about the ".expanded" suffix and sampling semantics.
Logan Wright (author): Added a TODO linking to ENG-9033 for runbook updates; will follow up with Rafael to land the doc change.
